## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Makkha Sutta* (Iti 5, PTS It 3), titled *Disdain* in the English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato, is the fifth discourse of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The short discourse presents a concise doctrinal teaching centered on overcoming the defilement of disdain or contempt (*makkha*): by fully abandoning this single quality, one is assured the spiritual attainment of non-return [SuttaCentral].

A direct parallel to the sutta is preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon in the *Itivuttaka* translation at T 765.18 (覆藏) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus aligns segments of the text with a discourse in the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (增壹阿含經, T 125, fascicle 6) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the sutta shares 26 textual matches with 11 other works, reflecting the formulaic framework characteristic of the *Itivuttaka*'s opening chapter [DharmaNexus]. Nearly the entire text (§0.1–4.1/4.2) is shared with adjacent discourses that address other unwholesome qualities, including the *Lobha Sutta* (Iti 1), *Dosa Sutta* (Iti 2), *Moha Sutta* (Iti 3), *Kodha Sutta* (Iti 4), and *Māna Sutta* (Iti 6), as well as corresponding discourses on full comprehension (*pariññā*, Iti 9–12) [DharmaNexus]. Segments of the discourse are also cited in the commentary (*Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā*) and the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].

None of the retrieved secondary reference passages discuss Iti 5 directly; rather, they cite or translate the term *makkha* as a generic psychological defilement (*upakkilesa*) or as one of Māra's armies in other canonical contexts.
